newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares close with focus on BTA, BPSM.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares close with focus on BTA, BPSM.

text.p: 1725 GMT - Portuguese shares closed with activity focused heavily on two banks of the Antonio Champalimaud group -- Banco Totta e Acores and Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor, which accounted for 40 percent of the total turnover of 8.3 billion escudos.
* Totta crashed over 10 percent in heavy trade after announcing on Friday night that it would pay out far less than investors had been expecting in dividends on its 1996 results.
Sister bank Banco Pinto took off in the other direction, soaring over eight percent after the Friday announcement pledged a higher payout than had been predicted.
The turmoil on the Lisbon bourse, with Banco Pinto stock being suspended at one point, led the chairman of the Champalimaud group which controls both banks to issue a call for calm.

Antonio Champalimaud, whose son Luis was named chairman of both banks in the reshuffle on Friday, said that there was no reason for Totta to fall so sharply. He warned investors who sold that they risked losing money.
He said that he personally would be demanding that the bank increase "significantly" the level of dividend that it was proposing to pay.
* Dealers said they expected BTA and BPSM to account for a lower share of overall turnover on Lisbon bourse tomorrow and that BTA would trade at around 2,700 escudos.

* "Tomorrow could see some activity in BTA and BPSM, but less than today. Today's reactions were very psychological with investors disillusioned with the proposed dividend for Totta," said one analyst.

He added: "The trend of the market tomorrow will depend to some extent on the close of Wall Street today. Interest will be concentrated on the usual 'blue chip' stocks such as Portugal Telecom and Cimpor."
* Other shares were well-supported, such as Somague, BES, Cimpor and preference shares in leisure group Lusomundo.
